lines.text: A calculator with just two buttons. Can you reach ninety in as few presses as possible?
lines.caption: A calculator with just two buttons. Can you reach ninety in as few presses as possible?

lines.text: Most kids start pressing forward and get lost. There's a much smarter direction.
lines.caption: Most kids start pressing forward and get lost. There's a much smarter direction.

lines.text: Hello, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this calculator.
lines.caption: Hello, I'm Vantee! Let's crack this calculator.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A calculator shows three.
lines.caption: A calculator shows three.

lines.text: It has only two keys. One adds one to the number on the screen.
lines.caption: It has only two keys. One adds one to the number on the screen.

lines.text: The other doubles the number on the screen.
lines.caption: The other doubles the number on the screen.

lines.text: What is the fewest number of key presses needed to make the screen show ninety?
lines.caption: What is the fewest number of key presses needed to make the screen show ninety?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? We start at three, and we want to end at ninety.
lines.caption: So what do we know? We start at three, and we want to end at ninety.

lines.text: Each press either adds one, or doubles.
lines.caption: Each press either adds one, or doubles.

lines.text: We don't just want a way to get there. We want the FEWEST presses.
lines.caption: We don't just want a way to get there. We want the FEWEST presses.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: work backwards, from ninety down to three.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: work backwards, from ninety down to three.

lines.text: Going backwards, doubling becomes halving, and adding one becomes taking one away.
lines.caption: Going backwards, doubling becomes halving, and adding one becomes taking one away.

lines.text: Halving is the big move, so halve whenever you can. If the number is odd, take one away first.
lines.caption: Halving is the big move, so halve whenever you can. If the number is odd, take one away first.

lines.text: Ninety is even, so cut it in half. That gives forty-five.
lines.caption: Ninety is even, so cut it in half. That gives forty-five.

lines.text: Forty-five is odd, so take one away: forty-four. Halve it: twenty-two. Halve again: eleven.
lines.caption: Forty-five is odd, so take one away: forty-four. Halve it: twenty-two. Halve again: eleven.

lines.text: Eleven is odd, so take one away: ten. Halve it: five.
lines.caption: Eleven is odd, so take one away: ten. Halve it: five.

lines.text: Five is odd, take one away: four. Now four is even, but half of four is two, and that's below three!
lines.caption: Five is odd, take one away: four. Now four is even, but half of four is two, and that's below three!

lines.text: So take one away instead. Four minus one is three. We made it!
lines.caption: So take one away instead. Four minus one is three. We made it!

lines.text: Read it forwards from three: every arrow is one key press.
lines.caption: Read it forwards from three: every arrow is one key press.

lines.text: Now count the arrows, not the numbers. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.
lines.caption: Now count the arrows, not the numbers. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.

lines.text: Eight presses. That's Choice C!
lines.caption: Eight presses. That's Choice C!

lines.text: Can anyone beat eight? Let's plan the doubles, and see why not.
lines.caption: Can anyone beat eight? Let's plan the doubles, and see why not.

lines.text: Five doubles is too many. Three doubled five times is ninety-six, already past ninety.
lines.caption: Five doubles is too many. Three doubled five times is ninety-six, already past ninety.

lines.text: With four doubles, three becomes forty-eight. We still need forty-two more.
lines.caption: With four doubles, three becomes forty-eight. We still need forty-two more.

lines.text: Here's the trick. A plus-one pressed early gets doubled later, like a snowball.
lines.caption: Here's the trick. A plus-one pressed early gets doubled later, like a snowball.

lines.text: A plus-one before all four doubles is worth sixteen. Before three doubles, eight. Then four, two, and one.
lines.caption: A plus-one before all four doubles is worth sixteen. Before three doubles, eight. Then four, two, and one.

lines.text: Make forty-two from those values: sixteen plus sixteen plus eight plus two. That's four adds.
lines.caption: Make forty-two from those values: sixteen plus sixteen plus eight plus two. That's four adds.

lines.text: Can three plus-one presses do it? The biggest three are sixteen, sixteen, sixteen: forty-eight, too big.
lines.caption: Can three plus-one presses do it? The biggest three are sixteen, sixteen, sixteen: forty-eight, too big.

lines.text: The next biggest is sixteen, sixteen, eight. That's forty, too small. Nothing in between!
lines.caption: The next biggest is sixteen, sixteen, eight. That's forty, too small. Nothing in between!

lines.text: So we need four doubles and four plus-one presses. That makes eight, and no fewer!
lines.caption: So we need four doubles and four plus-one presses. That makes eight, and no fewer!

lines.text: And it matches our chain: two plus-one presses at the start, one after the first double, one before the last.
lines.caption: And it matches our chain: two plus-one presses at the start, one after the first double, one before the last.

lines.text: With fewer doubles, it only gets worse. Three doubles would need nine adds. That's twelve presses.
lines.caption: With fewer doubles, it only gets worse. Three doubles would need nine adds. That's twelve presses.

lines.text: When would you pick each way? Work backwards to find a short path fast.
lines.caption: When would you pick each way? Work backwards to find a short path fast.

lines.text: Plan the doubles when you need to be sure nothing is shorter.
lines.caption: Plan the doubles when you need to be sure nothing is shorter.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice D, nine, counts the numbers in the chain. But the presses are the arrows between them, one fewer.
lines.caption: Choice D, nine, counts the numbers in the chain. But the presses are the arrows between them, one fewer.

lines.text: Choices A and B, six and seven, are too few. We showed you need four doubles and four adds.
lines.caption: Choices A and B, six and seven, are too few. We showed you need four doubles and four adds.

lines.text: Choice E, ten, can reach ninety, but it isn't the fewest. Two presses wasted!
lines.caption: Choice E, ten, can reach ninety, but it isn't the fewest. Two presses wasted!

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Count the steps, not the stops.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Count the steps, not the stops.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same calculator, same two keys, and it starts at three again.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same calculator, same two keys, and it starts at three again.

lines.text: This time, what's the fewest number of presses to reach one hundred?
lines.caption: This time, what's the fewest number of presses to reach one hundred?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's work backwards. One hundred, halve: fifty. Halve: twenty-five.
lines.caption: Let's work backwards. One hundred, halve: fifty. Halve: twenty-five.

lines.text: Twenty-five is odd, take one away: twenty-four. Then cut it in half three times: twelve, six, three!
lines.caption: Twenty-five is odd, take one away: twenty-four. Then cut it in half three times: twelve, six, three!

lines.text: Count the arrows: six presses.
lines.caption: Count the arrows: six presses.

lines.text: Check: five doubles take three to ninety-six, and one snowball add-one makes the last four. Six presses!
lines.caption: Check: five doubles take three to ninety-six, and one snowball add-one makes the last four. Six presses!

lines.text: Here's the sneaky part. The bigger target took fewer presses. If you got six, amazing work!
lines.caption: Here's the sneaky part. The bigger target took fewer presses. If you got six, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: To reach a target with doubling and adding one, work backwards.
lines.caption: To reach a target with doubling and adding one, work backwards.

lines.text: Cut it in half when it's even, unless that drops below the start.
lines.caption: Cut it in half when it's even, unless that drops below the start.

lines.text: Otherwise, take one away.
lines.caption: Otherwise, take one away.

lines.text: And count the presses, the arrows, not the numbers.
lines.caption: And count the presses, the arrows, not the numbers.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
